patternStatus: Read on 2026-09-16 from the rendered page, section "Data Grids For Presenting Tabular Information", "Keyboard Interaction - Setting Focus and Navigating Inside Cells" and "WAI-ARIA Roles, States, and Properties". The itemised comparison is in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-16-data-grid-design.md §2.
roleReason: The pattern's own words: a grid is a composite widget, it always contains multiple focusable elements, only one of them is in the page tab sequence, and the author manages focus inside it. That is the line docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-table-design.md §1 drew: table is the static structure and this family is the composite widget. The roles are written by hand — grid, rowgroup, row, columnheader, rowheader, gridcell — because the DOM is div, and the DOM is div because a row that is display: grid takes a track per column, which is what lets a column be resized live, pinned with sticky and left out of the DOM when it is off screen; table-layout gives none of the three.
rootReason: The root is the frame and the widget, and the scroller is one element in. The frame holds the border, the radius, the clip, the footer bar and every aria-* property the grid role carries; the scroller is the window the virtualiser measures and the box a sticky header and a pinned column resolve against. Unlike table, the family owns its height: a virtualised grid needs a viewport, and a grid without one grows to its content, stays correct and windows nothing.

data.rows: the consumer's array, read every render; the family never mutates it
data.rowKey: a field name or a function of the row; the key survives sorting, filtering, windowing and editing, and every state model names rows by it
data.columns: GridColumn[]: id, label, kind, accessor, format, compare, align, numeric, text, width, minWidth, maxWidth, flex, sortable, filterable, searchable, editable, resizable, reorderable, hideable, rowHeader, options, aggregate, validate, parse
data.columnGroups: GridColumnGroup[]: id, label and the ids it spans, drawn as a header row above the columns with aria-colspan
data.kind: a FilterKind of @slotted/core/filter — text, number, date, time, datetime, boolean, set — or actions or custom. It decides the operators, the comparator, the default alignment, the default editor and whether the column is searchable.
data.accessor: accessor(row) gives the domain value; format(value, row) gives the text. Sorting and filtering read the value; the cell draws the text. §2.9: a number, a currency and a date are values, not strings.
data.mode: client applies the query to rows with applyQuery; server reports the query and draws the rows it is given, reading totalCount or hasMore. Resolved to client when both are omitted.
data.reason: AG Grid, MUI X, Kendo, DevExtreme and Glide own the rows and apply the query; TanStack, React Aria, Fluent and Carbon leave it to the consumer. docs/build-order.md wave 9 decides it for this family: it applies the descriptor, and table reports.

query.shape: { sort: { column, direction }[], filter: FilterGroup | null, search: string, page: { index, size } | { cursor, size } | null, group: string[] }
query.one: One object, because a server receives one request, a URL holds one state and a saved view restores one value. Separate models — MUI X's sortModel, filterModel and paginationModel — make the consumer join them before every request and decide which moves first when a filter resets the page; here both happen in one transition and the request says what changed.
query.change: the request carries change: sort | filter | search | page | group beside the reason, so a consumer can refetch on sort and debounce on search without diffing two objects
query.resets: a change of filter, search or group puts page.index at 0 in the same transition

sort.keys: several; Shift while pressing a header appends, a plain press replaces; the cycle per key is ascending, descending, removed
sort.attribute: aria-sort on the first key's header only. The practice says aria-sort has limited value on more than one header because ARIA cannot say which key came first; the other keys carry a visible index and no property, and the announcement says the whole order.
sort.announce: the whole order, politely: 'Sorted by Customer, then by Date descending'

filter.evaluates: createFilterGroupPredicate over the whole group, nested groups included, because the grid evaluates whatever filter-bar wrote
filter.edits: one rule per column, in the header panel and in the filter row; a nested group is filter-bar's to edit and this family's to evaluate
filter.search: createSearchPredicate over the formatted text of every searchable column; the field that writes it is the consumer's text-field, the grid applies it

query.page: by index or by cursor. In client mode the family pages the array; in server mode it draws the page it is given. pagination draws the control in the footer; with a known total the footer says 1–50 of 3,412, without one it says 1–50 and offers load more.
query.group: column ids; group rows carry aria-level and aria-expanded, the value, the count and the column aggregates of their rows; one level or several
query.compare: column.compare replaces the kind's comparator: Intl.Collator(locale, { numeric: true }) for text, numeric for number, ISO text for date, time and datetime, false before true for boolean
query.serialization: toGridParams and fromGridParams compose toFilterBarParams for the filter and the search and add sort, page, size, cursor and group. Parsing is total: an unknown column, an unknown direction or a malformed page degrades to the default rather than to an error on first paint.
query.applies: applyQuery(rows, columns, query, { locale }) returns { rows, total, groups }: filter, search, sort, group, page, in that order. It is pure and exported from @slotted/core/grid so a consumer's server mock and the family agree.

columnState.shape: { order: string[], widths: Record<string, number>, hidden: string[], pinned: { start: string[], end: string[] } }
columnState.capability: columns, added to the shared vocabulary by this family
columnState.change: the request carries change: order | width | hidden | pinned beside the reason
columnState.normalizes: a state naming a column that no longer exists is normalised silently, because a saved view survives a removed column; a column the state does not name takes the model's own order and width
columnState.resize: the resizer on every resizable column's trailing edge, by pointer; Ctrl+Shift+ArrowLeft/Right by a step of --slotted-data-grid-resize-step with the cursor on the header, announced as the column and its width; Escape during a pointer drag restores. Bounded by minWidth and maxWidth. A double press on the resizer and Ctrl+Shift+Enter autofit the column to the cells in the DOM.
columnState.reorder: @slotted/core/drag: one horizontal container per pin zone, between targets, the header as the draggable and the handle; Alt+ArrowLeft/Right on the header is moveBy. A column never leaves its zone by dragging, because the zone is a fact of the state and a drop that changed two things would carry two reasons.
columnState.pin: by the column menu, and by the state. A pinned column is position: sticky with the summed width of the pinned columns before it as its inset; a header cell that is also pinned takes both offsets and the highest stacking step.
columnState.hide: by the column menu, and by the state. A hidden column leaves the DOM and the track; aria-colcount counts the visible columns of the model, so the numbers a reader hears are the columns they can reach.
columnState.manager: column-manager in wave 10 edits this object; until then the menu hides a column and the consumer writes the control that shows it again
columnState.serialization: serializeColumnState and parseColumnState round-trip the object through a string; parsing is total

cursor.shape: { row: string, column: string } | null, where row is a row key or one of the reserved words header, filter, summary, or group:<key>
cursor.tabStop: one: the current cell, or the single widget inside it; every other mounted cell is tabindex -1. Tab leaves the grid to the next control of the page.
cursor.focusInside: the two optimal combinations of the pattern, applied by rule: a cell whose content is exactly one focusable element that takes no arrow keys — a, button, input[type=checkbox], [role=switch], [role=button] — receives focus on that element; any other cell receives it on itself, Enter and F2 enter it, Escape leaves it, and Tab inside cycles the cell's widgets without leaving the cell
cursor.survives: when the current row disappears — a filter, a removal, a page — the cursor stays at the same row index or the last, in the same column; on an empty set focus goes to the empty part. The grid never drops focus to the document.
cursor.mounts: a key that moves the cursor to a row outside the virtual window scrolls the window so the row is mounted, then focuses it
cursor.paints: data-current on the cell and on its row; the ring is drawn inward, because a cell has no margin for an outer ring and the next row would cover it. Without focus the cursor stays at 60% so a reader returning from a popover finds where they were; with :focus-visible it is whole.

selection.rows: single and multiple select rows; the checkbox column is drawn, the row carries aria-selected and data-selected, Shift+Space on any cell toggles the row, Shift extends from the anchor, Ctrl+A selects every row the query left
selection.cells: range selects cells: { anchor, focus } | null; Shift+arrows extend, Shift+press sets, a pointer drag extends; every cell in the rectangle carries aria-selected and data-in-range, and the cells on its edges carry data-range-edge naming which edges. Ctrl+Space selects the column, Shift+Space the row, Ctrl+A every cell. No checkbox is drawn in this mode.
selection.copy: Ctrl+C writes the range — or the current cell — as tab-separated text through @slotted/core/clipboard, and announces the count. Paste is declined: docs/component-features.md §12 makes a spreadsheet its own product.
selection.selectAll: the header checkbox covers every row the query left, across every page in client mode and the page in server mode, and states which in its own accessible name; it is indeterminate while some are selected

value.range: { anchor: { row, column }, focus: { row, column } } | null

selection.multiselectable: aria-multiselectable="true" on the root in multiple and range
selection.columnWidth: --slotted-data-grid-selection-size, stated rather than shrink-wrapped so a column pinned beside it has a length to state

activation.when: a double press on a cell that does not edit, or Enter on a text cell of a row while activatable is true; with activatable and an editable cell, Enter edits and the double press activates
activation.notState: nothing stays, so it is an event and not a model; it is the fourth capability table deferred here by name, because a tr cannot be a widget and a grid cell can

editing.session: startEdit(cell) and stopEdit({ commit }) on the handle; onEditStart, onEditCommit and onEditCancel as events. The draft lives in the editor: a controlled draft would make the consumer re-render the grid on every keystroke of a field it does not own. MUI X has cellModesModel and limits it to custom triggers, which startEdit covers.

modes.cell: Enter, F2, a double press or an alphanumeric key open the cell's editor; Enter commits and moves one row down in the same column, Tab commits and moves to the next editable cell of the row, Shift+Tab back, F2 commits and stays, Escape cancels
modes.row: every editable cell of the row opens; Enter commits the row, Escape cancels the row, Tab moves between the row's editors, and Save and Cancel stand in the actions column while the row edits

editors.set: select, or multi-select when the column's value is an array

editing.plain: the editor is the field family in variant plain and size sm, and the cell hands it its inset: padding 0 on the cell and --slotted-control-padding-inline-* set to the cell's own inset, the rule table's cell already applies. The edited value stands where the read value stood.
editing.validate: column.validate(value, row) returns a message, null or a Promise of either. While pending the cell is data-loading; with a message the cell is data-invalid, aria-invalid and aria-errormessage point at the message, and the draft stays in the editor.
editing.commit: onEditCommit({ key, column, value, previous, row, reason }) may return a Promise. While pending the cell shows the new value and data-loading; if it rejects, the previous value returns, the editor reopens with the draft and the cell is data-invalid with the error's message. An error never discards what the reader typed — §12 says so by name.
editing.conflict: a change in rows to the cell being edited marks the cell data-invalid with labels.editConflict and leaves the draft untouched; onEditCommit receives previous — the value when the editor opened — and the consumer decides
editing.readonly: aria-readonly="true" on the root when no column edits; on a cell that does not edit when others do; on nothing when nothing edits, which is what the pattern requires
editing.typeToEdit: an alphanumeric key on an editable text or number cell opens the editor with that key as its first character, which is the pattern's own convention and what every spreadsheet does

expansion.detail: expanded as a set of row keys; the expander is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls; the detail row is one row with one cell spanning every column through aria-colspan; it is not rendered while closed
expansion.groups: expandedGroups as a set of group keys or the word all, which is the default: a grouped listing opens expanded, because a reader who grouped wants to see the groups' rows. A group key is column=value per level joined by /.
expansion.keys: ArrowRight on a group row opens it, ArrowLeft closes it, as in a tree grid; the same on the expander's cell of a row with a detail

virtualization.rows: the body takes block-size of the total and padding-block-start of the window's start offset; the mounted rows follow in flow. No transform, so position: sticky on a pinned column resolves against the scroller with nothing in between.
virtualization.columns: a window over the accumulated widths of the unpinned columns; the pinned ones are always mounted; every cell writes grid-column explicitly because auto-placement would move the cells that are there into the tracks of the cells that are not
virtualization.auto: virtualize auto windows rows above 100 and columns above 20; true always; false never
virtualization.rowHeight: a number, or auto. With a number the family trusts it and corrects it once from the first mounted row; with auto every mounted row is measured and createRowMetrics holds the sizes, bounded by --slotted-data-grid-row-max-block-size.
virtualization.ids: the row key is the row's identity and the cursor names it, so a row leaving and re-entering the window keeps its selection, its expansion and its focus
virtualization.loadMore: shouldLoadMore over the window; onLoadMore when fewer than loadMoreThreshold rows remain below the window; hasMore decides whether the footer offers it
virtualization.counts: aria-rowcount is the query's total, or -1 when unknown; aria-rowindex on every row counts the header rows first; aria-colcount and aria-colindex are always written because the DOM never holds every column

filter.shape: a trigger in the column-actions slot and a compact panel it opens; and, with filterRow, a row under the header with one operand per filterable column
filter.form: One condition is one line: [operator] [operand], controls in size sm, the operator at --slotted-data-grid-filter-operator-size and the operand taking the rest; between puts both operands on the same line with a dash. The join is two words in a segmented-control where the second line's operator would stand, shown once the first condition is active. The footer is Clear in ghost and Apply in solid, both sm, at the trailing edge. No title: the trigger names the column and the panel opens under it.
filter.formReason: table's panel stacks the operator, the operand, the join and two md buttons at full width, and the invocation refuses that form in writing. The form decided here is inherited by table and filter-bar in reopenings recorded in docs/build-order.md, so the three places a filter is edited share one geometry.
filter.row: filterRow draws a row under the header inside the head rowgroup: role row, one gridcell per column, the cursor reaches it with the arrows. Each cell holds the kind's operand in variant plain and size sm filling the cell, with the operator as a symbol button at the start of the field that opens a menu naming the operators in full. Text and number apply after filterDebounce and on Enter; the others on change. A set draws select with multiple, whose trigger summarises the chosen values; a boolean a select of any, yes, no.
filter.rowReason: AG Grid, MUI X, Kendo and DevExtreme ship it, and it is the densest form a wide listing has. table declined it because it cost a row of a static structure; here the row is part of the composite widget and the cursor walks it.
filter.symbols: ⊃ ⊅ = ≠ ^ $ > ≥ < ≤ ↔ ∅ ∄ and the kind's own words for is, is not, before, after, any of, none of. They are typographic characters with meaning rather than icons — the criterion that lets kbd write ⌘ — and the button's accessible name says the operator in full.
filter.set: select with multiple in the panel and in the row, its trigger summarising the chosen values and its options carrying counts per value from the rows the query left before this column's own rule, because here the grid owns the data and can count
filter.draft: the panel edits a draft: nothing reaches the query until Apply, Escape and a press outside restore what the panel opened with, Clear empties the draft. The filter row applies as it goes, which is what a row is for.
filter.marks: data-filtered on the column header and on its trigger; the trigger's accessible name states the applied summary through describeFilter
filter.announces: the summary on Apply, the removal on Clear, the count the query leaves after the filter row applies
filter.composition: popover holds the panel, select the operator, segmented-control the join, text-field, number-field, date-field, time-field, datetime-field, multi-select and select the operands, menu the row's operator, button the actions
filter.replaceable: the operand area, per column, through renderFilter in React and *slDataGridFilter in Angular; the draft, the operator, the join, the actions and the announcements stay

loading.first: with no rows to keep, the loader part draws skeleton rows the visible columns wide and skeletonRows deep
loading.refresh: over rows already shown, aria-busy goes on the root and the body dims; nothing moves
loading.reason: Carbon draws a skeleton and Ant dims what is there; they are two states, and a family with one answer gets the other wrong

states.no-results: the query left nothing; offers clear filters, which empties query.filter and query.search in one change with reason clear
states.error: loading failed; offers retry, which calls onRetry

empty.reason: the grid applies the filter, so it knows which of the three it is; AG Grid has one overlay and MUI X two

sticky.header: head, including the filter row; on by default because the family owns its height, so there is always a scroller with a header to pin
sticky.summary: the aggregate row, pinned to the end of the same box

to.scroll: the default: the family's own scroller
to.page: the nearest scrolling ancestor outside the family; the family gives up its own vertical scroll and therefore its row virtualisation, and the header stops at --slotted-data-grid-sticky-offset

sticky.columns: position: sticky with inset-inline-start or inset-inline-end, so a right-to-left document mirrors it
sticky.corner: a header cell that is also pinned takes both offsets and the highest stacking step, stated once

aggregates.custom: a function of the column's values
aggregates.where: the summary row for the whole query, and each group row for its own rows
aggregates.format: the column's format, so a currency column sums as a currency

wiring.aria-label: the consumer's, required by the types as label or labelledBy: a grid with no name is a widget a reader cannot find
wiring.aria-describedby: the consumer's, passed through untouched; the family appends the drag instructions id on a reorderable header
wiring.aria-sort: on the first sort key's header, and on no other
wiring.aria-selected: on a selected row, and on every cell of a range
wiring.aria-multiselectable: true on the root in multiple and range
wiring.aria-readonly: on the root when no column edits; on a cell that does not edit when others do
wiring.aria-rowcount: the query's total, or -1 when unknown, always
wiring.aria-rowindex: on every row, counting the header rows first, always
wiring.aria-colcount: the visible columns of the model, always
wiring.aria-colindex: on every cell, always, because the DOM never holds every column
wiring.aria-colspan: on a column group, a detail cell and a group row's cell
wiring.aria-expanded: on a group row, and on the expander with aria-controls naming the detail row
wiring.aria-busy: true on the root while loading over rows already shown
wiring.aria-invalid: on a cell whose draft failed, with aria-errormessage naming the message
wiring.tabindex: 0 on the current cell or its single widget, -1 on every other mounted cell

keyboard.effect: enters the grid on the current cell — the last visited, or the first cell of the body — and leaves it to the next control of the page
keyboard.focus: the current cell, or the single widget inside it

keyboard.effect: moves one cell to the right; on the last cell of the row it does not move; mirrored in a right-to-left document
the mirror of ArrowRight
moves one cell down; from the header to the filter row, then the body; on the last row it does not move; mounts the row when it is outside the window
moves one cell up; from the first body row to the filter row and the header; on the first header row it does not move
moves down one view of rows, scrolling; on the last row it does not move
moves up one view of rows, scrolling; on the first row it does not move
moves to the first cell of the row
moves to the last cell of the row
moves to the first cell of the first body row
moves to the last cell of the last row the query left, mounting it
in range mode, selects the whole column; otherwise nothing
in single and multiple, toggles the row; in range, selects the whole row
in multiple, selects every row the query left; in range, every cell; otherwise nothing
in range, extends the range one cell to the right from the anchor
in range, extends the range one cell to the left
in range, extends the range one cell down; in multiple, extends the row selection from the anchor
the mirror of Shift+ArrowDown
on an editable cell, opens the editor; on a cell with widgets, focuses the first; on a text cell of an activatable row, activates it; on a column header, sorts the column
keyboard.focus: the editor, the widget, or the cell

keyboard.effect: opens the editor or enters the cell; a second F2 commits the draft and returns to the cell
on an editable text or number cell, opens the editor with the key as its first character
in an editor, cancels the draft and returns to the cell; in a widget, returns to the cell; with a range, clears it; during a drag, drag takes it
commits and moves one row down in the same column in cell mode; commits the row in row mode
keyboard.focus: the cell below, or the same cell

keyboard.effect: commits and moves to the next editable cell of the row; Shift+Tab back; on the last, commits and stays
toggles the row's checkbox; Shift+Space extends from the anchor
appends the column to the sort order instead of replacing it
opens the column menu
keyboard.focus: the first item of the menu, then back to the header

keyboard.effect: widens the column by one step, announced
narrows the column by one step, announced
fits the column to its mounted cells
moves the column one position later, through drag.moveBy
moves the column one position earlier

keyboard.where: on a group row, or on the expander cell of a row with a detail
keyboard.effect: opens the group or the detail; when already open, moves right as usual

keyboard.where: on an open group row, or on the expander cell of an open detail
keyboard.effect: closes it; when already closed, moves left as usual
copies the range, or the current cell, as tab-separated text; not intercepted while the page holds a text selection

keyboardReason: Every key of the pattern's data grid table is answered, plus the selection keys it lists as commonly used and the three conventions of its inside-a-cell section. The departures are the column operations — resize, reorder, menu, append to sort — that the pattern does not cover and that React Aria, Fluent and the practice's resizing note each answer differently, and the two spreadsheet conventions, Enter moving down and Ctrl+C.

Enter.reason: Excel, AG Grid and MUI X move one row down on commit, and a reader entering a column of values expects it
Enter.cost: a reader who wants to commit and stay uses F2 or Tab

Shift+Enter.reason: Shift+press is how AG Grid and MUI X append a sort key with the pointer; the same modifier on the keyboard keeps one gesture
Shift+Enter.cost: none found: Shift+Enter has no meaning on a column header otherwise

Ctrl+Enter.reason: a column menu needs a key, and Ctrl+Enter is the one MUI X uses

Ctrl+Shift+Arrow.reason: resizing needs a keyboard equivalent (§2.8 of docs/component-features.md); React Aria and Fluent use arrows on a focused resizer, and this family has no focusable resizer because a resizer in the tab sequence of a composite widget would be a second stop
Ctrl+Shift+Arrow.cost: only with the cursor on a column header, where there is no editor; in an editor the combination stays the browser's own word selection

Alt+Arrow.reason: decided in @slotted/core/drag: moveBy is the APG one-call reorder
Alt+Arrow.cost: Alt+ArrowLeft is back in some browsers; only with the cursor on a header, and preventDefault stops the navigation

Ctrl+C.reason: a range with no copy is a range nobody needed; AG Grid, MUI X and Glide all copy
Ctrl+C.cost: takes the page's copy while focus is in the grid; with a non-empty text selection the family does not intercept

ArrowRight/ArrowLeft on a group row.reason: the tree grid pattern; a group row is a node
ArrowRight/ArrowLeft on a group row.cost: the first press on a closed group opens it rather than moving; the second moves

tableElement.reason: a grid resizes columns live, pins them with sticky and leaves them out of the DOM off screen; display: grid gives a row all three and table-layout gives none. The pattern admits both constructions.

paste.reason: docs/component-features.md §12 makes a spreadsheet its own product: pasting into a range is a bulk write with no per-cell validation

export.composition: getVisibleRows() on the handle, and two lines of the consumer's for a CSV

filterChips.composition: filter-bar above the grid, reading and writing query.filter
filterChips.reason: one descriptor, two families: the chips draw what the grid evaluates

filterBuilder.reason: nesting and groups are section 12's Filter Builder; the grid evaluates them and does not edit them

columnManagerPanel.reason: wave 10; the grid exposes columnState, which is what that panel edits

dragBetweenPinZones.composition: the column menu pins and unpins
dragBetweenPinZones.reason: the zone is a fact of the state; a drop that changed both position and zone would carry two reasons

controlledEditSession.composition: startEdit and stopEdit on the handle
controlledEditSession.reason: a controlled draft re-renders the grid on every keystroke of a field the consumer does not own

ariaSortOnEveryKey.composition: aria-sort on the first key, a visible index on the others, the whole order announced
ariaSortOnEveryKey.reason: the practice says aria-sort has limited value on more than one header

size.reason: as table: the theme restates the control scale per density and the row reads it

focusableResizer.reason: a resizer in the tab sequence of a composite widget is a second tab stop, which the pattern forbids

autoHeightVirtualization.reason: a window needs a viewport; without one the grid grows to its content and stays correct

print.reason: rows outside the DOM do not print, and releasing the window under @media print would mount every row of a hundred thousand

labels.selectAllPage: Select the {count} rows on this page
labels.editConflict: This value changed while you were editing
labels.editFailed: The change could not be saved
labels.noResults: No rows match the current filters
labels.error: The rows could not be loaded

labelsReason: Every word the family says, in one input rather than one prop each: an application translates them once. The operator names and symbols are two maps keyed by the engine's operator, because a map is what filter-bar and table already read for the same operators.

sort.scope: the query, not a sort of its own: sort, filter, search, page and group are one object because a server receives one request and a URL holds one state. The request carries change: sort | filter | search | page | group beside the reason. sort and filter declare the same model on purpose; the schema checks each model's shape and the contract says here why the two are one.

filter.scope: the same query object as sort, for the reason written there

columns.scope: order, widths, hidden and pinned in one object, because a saved view restores one value and column-manager edits one object. The request carries change: order | width | hidden | pinned.
